stemMd: Controlled oxidation of a primary alcohol can first produce which functional group?

options.label: A
options.textMd: An amide without a nitrogen source

explanationMd: Removing hydrogen from a primary alcohol forms a terminal carbonyl, an aldehyde. Further oxidation can yield a carboxylic acid, so conditions matter when isolating the intermediate.

distractorRationale.d: Chemical oxidation cannot create a different element.
distractorRationale.e: Ether formation is not the defining primary-alcohol oxidation step.
distractorRationale.a: Nitrogen cannot appear without a source.
distractorRationale.b: Oxidation does not simply remove oxygen and reduce the molecule.
